title: Plant trainer, first test: can you tell the shipped herb from one the trainer rebuilt?
question: One side is the shipped herb. The other is a herb whose photosynthesis was cut in half and then rebuilt by the trainer in 10 generations. Pick the one you think is the shipped herb — or say in the comment that you can't tell.
context_md:
The **plant trainer's acceptance test** (breeding species files instead of writing them; herb first, in the lab bed).

I crippled a copy of the herb (both photosynthesis rates halved) and let the trainer change only its leaf numbers. It brought them back: shoot 0.275 -> 0.44 (shipped 0.55), leaf 0.225 -> 0.49 (shipped 0.45), and it settled on 5 leaves a node instead of 8.

Each side is **three lab beds**, each shown at frame 8,000 (one young herb) and frame 40,000 (the herb and its seedlings). Same beds, same seeds on both sides.

Measured on 12 beds read once: shipped **3.88**, crippled start **3.33**, rebuilt **3.80** (inside the shipped herb's noise), and the same run with parents picked at random **3.42**. One run each, so this is a first pass, not a verdict on the trainer.
